blocks.content: Plate Tectonics explains the movement of continents through convection currents in the asthenosphere, rectifying the main flaw in Wegener's Continental Drift theory.

rows: Continents plow directly through oceanic crust like icebergs.
Rigid lithospheric plates float and move across the asthenosphere.
Thermal convection currents in the mantle
Jigsaw fit of coastlines, Glossopteris fossils, tillite deposits
Seafloor spreading, paleomagnetism, mid-ocean ridge mapping

items: Wegener incorrectly identified 'pole-fleeing force' (centrifugal force due to Earth's rotation) and 'tidal force' as the drivers of continental movement—a popular trap in UPSC Prelims.
Memorize the 7 major plates: Pacific, North American, South American, Eurasian, African, Indo-Australian, and Antarctic.
Seafloor spreading theory proposed by Harry Hess in 1960 acted as the vital conceptual bridge connecting Continental Drift to Plate Tectonics.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Alfred Wegener proposed the Continental Drift theory in 1912, hypothesizing that all present-day continents were once part of a single supercontinent named Pangea surrounded by the ocean Panthalassa.
Continental Drift was initially rejected by the scientific community because Wegener could not provide a plausible physical mechanism to explain how continents moved.

Plate Tectonics theory, formulated in 1967 by McKenzie, Parker, and Morgan, posits that the Earth's rigid lithosphere is broken into major and minor plates that float over the semi-fluid asthenosphere.
Thermal convection currents within the Earth's mantle serve as the primary driving mechanism for lithospheric plate movements.
Discoveries in seafloor spreading by Harry Hess and paleomagnetism provided the crucial empirical foundation for Plate Tectonics.
